title: NHTSA says car crashes are a leading cause of death for children ages 1 to 13
summary: NHTSA says car seats and boosters protect infants and children in a crash, and that car crashes are a leading cause of death for children ages 1 to 13.
body: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration's car-seat page says car seats and booster seats provide protection in a crash, yet car crashes are a leading cause of death for children ages 1 to 13. It says to choose a seat for the child's age and size, use a seat that fits the vehicle, and use it every time. A separate line on the page says that in 2024, 39 percent of children killed in car crashes were unrestrained, and that car seats saved 325 children under 5 in one year. Those two figures are what the page displays. This card does not open the tables behind the word Source. WHO's road-injury sheet uses a different age band. The US sentence here is ages 1 to 13.
